scope: Unreleased Bukkit source correction for delayed challenge ordering. No product JAR build or live Minecraft execution in this validation.

issue.before: The initial two-tick task captured A. A reload could send B first, then the task sent A last. Companion generation coalescing could discard B; an A response remains stale and strict verification times out.
issue.after: The production scheduled Runnable checks the same Player owner and online status, then retrieves the currently pending challenge at execution time.

validation.compiled: All current core and Bukkit production Java sources, including the plugin scheduling call, plus PendingChallengeTaskTest, against the pinned Spigot 1.8.8 API.
checks: Old-closure negative-control model sends stale A and real GuardService expires it at the strict deadline. This is not execution of the historical Bukkit plugin binary.
Actual production task sends B after reload replaces A, and the real GuardService accepts B and does not time out.
A removed pending challenge is not resent.
A disconnected owner cannot send retained pending bytes.
An old Player task cannot send the replacement session challenge, even when the former owner still appears online.
An offline owner cannot send pending bytes.
scopeLimits: The scheduler and Player identity are provided as deterministic suppliers; no Bukkit server or real client was started.
The old behavior is a model copied from the prior closure. Only the fixed production Runnable and current GuardService execute in the positive checks.
Gradle check wiring was added but was not executed during this low-resource Java8 validation.

privacy: Only source paths, compiler/runtime output, and synthetic test descriptions are public. Test state directories, account/device state, and actual identifiers are excluded.
